name: Electrician
title: Free Electrician Invoice Template
description: A free electrician invoice template: labor by task, materials, equipment, and permit fees as a separate charge. Fill it in online and download a PDF.
summary: Labor by task, materials and permit fees, laid out for service calls and installations.
intro: Each task, each material and the permit fee on its own line, so a homeowner or a business owner can match the invoice to your quote. Fill it in online and download a PDF.
explanation: Electrical work is easy to describe badly. “Electrical work, 12 hours” tells the client nothing; “Upgrade main panel to 200 A” and “Install EV charger circuit, 60 A” tell them exactly what they paid for, and help the next electrician too.

This template uses Folio’s contractor layout: labor, materials and equipment in subtotalled sections. Permit and inspection fees go in the separate charge line beneath the tax, because they are a pass-through cost rather than your work.
It works for residential service calls, panel upgrades, rewiring, EV chargers, lighting and small commercial jobs.
fieldsTitle: What to put on an electrician invoice

fields.name: Job and address
fields.text: What the job was and where: “Panel upgrade and EV charger — 418 Juniper Street”.

fields.name: Labor by task
fields.text: One line per task with hours at your rate. Naming the circuit, the amperage or the room makes the invoice useful as a record of the work.

fields.name: Materials
fields.text: Panels, breakers, wire, conduit and devices. Group small items into one line (“Wire, conduit and fittings”) unless the client asked for detail.

fields.name: Equipment
fields.text: Rented lifts or trenchers billed to the job.

fields.name: Permits and inspection
fields.text: The permit fee as a separate charge. In the generator, use Shipping or other charge and rename it “Permit and inspection”.

fields.name: License number
fields.text: Your electrical contractor license number, in the Tax ID field, where your state or city expects it on paperwork.

fields.name: Warranty and notes
fields.text: Your workmanship guarantee and anything the client should know, such as the date the inspection passed.

steps.title: Open the example
steps.text: Customize this invoice opens a panel upgrade in the generator. Replace the client, the address and the tasks.

steps.title: List the work
steps.text: Add each task under Labor and each material under Materials. Subtotals are worked out for you.

steps.title: Add the permit
steps.text: Put the permit fee in Shipping or other charge and rename it. It is added after tax.

steps.title: Download and send
steps.text: Check the preview, download the PDF and send it. Your numbering continues on the next invoice.

faqs.q: How should an electrician show permit fees on an invoice?
faqs.a: As a separate line, named, at the amount you paid. In Folio, the Shipping or other charge field can be renamed “Permit and inspection”; it is added after tax, which suits a fee you are passing through.

faqs.q: Should I itemize materials or give one total?
faqs.a: Itemize anything significant (a panel, a charger, a fixture) and group the small parts. Clients and insurers look for the big items; nobody wants forty lines of wire nuts.

faqs.q: Can I bill a flat rate instead of hours?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter a quantity of 1 and your flat price for the task, e.g. “Install EV charger circuit, flat rate”. You can mix flat-rate and hourly lines on one invoice.
That depends on your state and the type of work; in many states materials are taxable and labor is not. Check with your state tax agency and enter the rate that applies.
